symptom: `mxcli marketplace install <id>` of a module or widget that ships pluggable widgets left the project failing CE0463 (41 units in the field run) until the user ran `mxcli fix widgets` by hand; install only printed it as a "Next" step
cause: `installModuleFromFile` (transplant path) and the widget paths (`installWidget`, `placeWidgetFile` via `printWidgetNext`) printed the `mxcli fix widgets` / `mxcli fix design-properties` commands instead of running them
insight: A step every install needs and only one tool can do belongs in the install, not in its output: a printed "Next" is skipped by agents and humans alike. The repair reuses `docker.RunToolPreservingFormat` (what `mxcli fix` calls), so MPR v2 survives; bare `mx update-widgets` would collapse it. Unresolvable mx (or an unreadable version) keeps the printed commands as a warning, never a failure, and a failing step names its own manual command while the next still runs. Measured on 11.6.6 with `install --file` of a widget: update-widgets ran, 369 .mxunit files before and after. Not changed: `marketplace update` (still prints the steps) and the --allow-format-change module-import path; dependency resolution is a separate concern
